contract_findings.evidence: GET /proctor-assignments/me accepts PROCTOR only and derives proctorPublicId and tenantId from CurrentUserContext. The repository predicate includes both identities and deterministic opensAt/publicId ordering.
contract_findings.resolution: The Flutter client can discover only the authenticated proctor's tenant-scoped assignments without user or tenant override parameters.

contract_findings.evidence: Inbound SUBSCRIBE and SEND frames are authorized by destination, role, tenant, assignment and ACTIVE session state. Direct sends to broker destinations are rejected.
contract_findings.resolution: Assigned PROCTOR can control, same-tenant HOST_ADMIN can subscribe read-only, and HOST_AUTHOR cannot access live session topics.

contract_findings.evidence: COMMAND_ACCEPTED and VIOLATION_DETECTED broadcasts use the typed eventId/eventType/sessionPublicId/occurredAt/data envelope.
contract_findings.resolution: Flutter receives a stable live contract while existing outbox and Kafka event payloads remain unchanged.

contract_findings.evidence: A PROCTOR REST recovery query requires an ACTIVE locally owned proctor session before the tenant-scoped violation snapshot is returned. HOST_ADMIN retains tenant-scoped audit access.
contract_findings.resolution: Reconnect recovery cannot be used by an unassigned proctor to read another live session.

contract_findings.evidence: docker compose ps returned no running services; the compose file does not start the application services.
contract_findings.resolution: Start gateway, IAM, scheduling and proctor with fixtures, then demonstrate the approved three-role authorization matrix and one real violation event.
